query: Implement the use case enroll(profileId, courseId) in src/data for RF-PRG-01. Clicking 'Começar o curso' twice must not create two enrollments.
expected_behavior: Starts from the session gate and confirms the profile belongs to the session's user in the query itself (owner-scoped), not only in a separate check
Writes with insert ... onConflictDoNothing (or onConflictDoUpdate) targeting the unique (profile_id, course_id) key instead of a select-then-insert
Returns the existing enrollment on the second call with no error
Tests against a real Postgres (service container or Docker) calling enroll twice, and with another user's profile id, without mocking Drizzle

query: Rename the column courses.level to courses.difficulty.
expected_behavior: Classifies the rename as a contract change and splits it into an expand PR now and a contract PR later
The expand PR adds difficulty, backfills it with an idempotent custom migration (WHERE difficulty IS NULL), and moves reads and writes to difficulty
Leaves dropping level to the later contract PR and says so in the ticket comment
Reads the generated SQL and confirms no statement drops data; never edits an already applied migration

query: Implement catalog search by course title and author name, ignoring case and accents, for RF-CAT-02.
expected_behavior: Normalizes the term with the same normalizeSearchText function that writes courses.search_text
Escapes % and _ in the term and queries search_text with ilike, served by the GIN trigram index using extensions.gin_trgm_ops
Takes the catalog scope as an argument and applies the RN-04 child restriction in the WHERE clause
Paginates 24 per page with a stable order ending in id, and calls no unaccent() at query time

query: When a lesson is marked complete, recompute whether the course is completed (RN-03) and send the student a congratulations e-mail when it is.
expected_behavior: Runs the progress write and the completion recalculation in one db.transaction, every statement on tx
Reads the rows the completion depends on with .for('update') inside the transaction
Sends the e-mail after the commit, inside after(), never inside the transaction
Tests that a failure inside the transaction leaves neither the progress row nor the completion behind
